stem.en: Spirit alcohol, the alcohol in spirit lamps, has a carbon score of minus 2 on average, and it burns with 30 kilojoules per gram, less than octane's 47. Kabir says "so the scoreboard is wrong, both are minus 2". What did he miss?

text.en: Spirit alcohol carries an oxygen atom that adds mass to the gram without adding fall. Per carbon, both fall similarly; per gram, spirit alcohol has fewer carbons to fall.

feedback.en: The score predicts fall per carbon. Heat per gram also depends on how many carbons are in the gram.
Its bonds are ordinary carbon-hydrogen and carbon-oxygen bonds. The oxygen it carries is the difference.
Octane is simply all hydrocarbon. There is nothing in the gram that is not fuel.

explanation.en: Two things set heat per gram: how far each carbon falls, and how many carbons the gram holds. Oxygen already on the molecule reduces the second.
